key_insight: A black-box attack called immrag can extract many distinct images from multimodal retrieval systems by using an attacker image plus a previously recovered image to steer retrieval toward new items.
clinical_relevance: For medical imaging tools that rely on multimodal retrieval, this highlights a privacy and security risk that could expose sensitive radiology images if safeguards are weak.
method: Uses image-returning multimodal RAG, where the retrieved visual artifact is the response
Blends a shadow image with a recovered image to form each query
Applies relevance-weighted resampling to move through embedding space and find novel retrievals
evidence_signal: In 2,500-query runs, the attack reconstructed up to 611 radiology images, 566 document scans, and 416 general-purpose images, reaching up to 5.6x more distinct datastore items than a non-adaptive baseline.
watch_item: The results come from controlled experiments on specific retrievers and generators, so real-world risk will depend on system design, access controls, and whether additional defenses are in place.
paper_title: Walking the Embedding Space: Datastore Extraction from Multimodal RAG
